title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026. College Wednesday night review: Buffalo at Ball State, Sacramento State at Central Michigan and Massachusetts at Toledo (Nov. 11), graded. Then the rest of the college week.

paragraphs: Wednesday put three more MAC games on the board, and all three are final. The one that hurts came in Mount Pleasant. Sacramento State +18.5 was covering by 4.5 with two minutes left, went for it on fourth down at its own 10, came up empty, and Townsend's 6-yard touchdown run with 1:05 left beat the Hornets ticket by 2.5. Toledo −14.5 had it won by halftime against Massachusetts, and Buffalo −1.5 pulled away late at Ball State after three missed Ball State field goals. All three Overs died. Two of the three games finished with 35 points, and the third finished with 24.

Every game below is graded against the line printed on the card at kickoff, using ESPN finals and play-by-play, and a push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. The Cover Writer's numbers held all day: Buffalo −1.5 and the Over 50.5, projecting Buffalo 28, Ball State 25; Sacramento State +18.5 and the Over 43.5, projecting Central Michigan 30, Sacramento State 16; and Toledo −14.5 and the Over 51.5, projecting Toledo 34, Massachusetts 19.

Letdown Watch posted its own numbers in three spots and is graded on them: Buffalo −2.5 and the Under 51.5 in Muncie, Sacramento State +17.5, and the Under 52.5 in Toledo. Follow The Money took Ball State +1.5 and had no other picks. In The Trenches took Ball State +1.5 and Central Michigan −18.5, had no side in Toledo and had no totals. The Formula and Next Man Up made picks on all three games.

Card line: Central Michigan −18.5, total 43.5. The Cover Writer's card had Sacramento State +18.5 and the Over, projecting Central Michigan 30, Sacramento State 16. Final: Sacramento State 7, Central Michigan 28. Central Michigan won by 21, and the teams scored 35 points.

Sacramento State +18.5 was the ticket that looked like a winner for 58 minutes. Clerveaux broke a 27-yard touchdown run for Central Michigan in the first quarter, Ene answered with a 37-yarder for the Hornets, and only Blue's 8-yard run with 19 seconds left in the half put the Chippewas up 14-7 at the break. The Hornets were covering by 11.5, and the total sat at 21, 22.5 short of the Over 43.5.

Townsend ran 40 yards for a touchdown midway through the third, 21-7, and Sacramento State +18.5 was still covering by 4.5. Then the Hornets got a gift: Silvera punched the ball loose from Clerveaux at the Sacramento State 38, and the Hornets recovered. Central Michigan went more than 20 minutes of game clock without another point, punting twice from Hornets territory in the fourth. Every Hornets ticket only needed the clock to keep running. The Over 43.5 needed 15.5 more points from two offenses that had stopped scoring, and it was gone long before the end.

Then came the call that will haunt every Hornets backer. Down 14 with under two minutes left, pinned deep after a 35-yard punt to the 5, Sacramento State went for it on fourth down from its own 10. Salazar's deep throw for Taylor fell incomplete under pressure, and Central Michigan took over 10 yards from the end zone. Two Townsend runs later, the 6-yard touchdown landed with 1:05 left. Central Michigan 28, Sacramento State 7. A 21-point margin, and Sacramento State +18.5 lost by 2.5 after covering for 58 minutes. Letdown Watch's +17.5 lost by 3.5. In The Trenches on Central Michigan −18.5 got a cover it had every reason to give up on, and the Under 43.5 crowd never broke a sweat.
Called it: In The Trenches on Central Michigan −18.5, covered by 2.5 points. Next Man Up on the Under 43.5, stayed under by 8.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on Sacramento State +18.5, missed by 2.5 points. Letdown Watch on Sacramento State +17.5, missed by 3.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Over 43.5, fell 8.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the total.

items.matchup: College Wednesday · No sweat against the number

paragraphs: Card line: Toledo −14.5, total 51.5. The Cover Writer's card had Toledo −14.5 and the Over, projecting Toledo 34, Massachusetts 19. Final: Massachusetts 0, Toledo 24. Toledo won by 24, and the teams scored 24 points.

Toledo −14.5 was cashed by halftime, and the Over 51.5 never got off the ground. Toledo opened by coming up empty on fourth down at the UMass 28, then Walendzak went 69 yards for a touchdown. Hammer's 74-yard punt return for another one came back on an illegal block, Griffith made a 27-yard field goal, and Thompson picked off Inagawa and went 62 yards the other way. 17-0. Massachusetts +14.5 backers got one chance at life on the next kickoff, and Magee took it 98 yards to the end zone before a UMass holding flag wiped it out. Richter hit Walendzak for 17 yards and a touchdown at 1:51, and it was 24-0 at the half. Toledo −14.5 was covering by 9.5, and the total sat at 24, 27.5 short of the Over 51.5.

The second half was scoreless. UMass turned it over on downs at the Toledo 26 right before the break, at the Toledo 23 early in the fourth and again at the Toledo 40. Even a UMass touchdown on the drive that died at the Toledo 23 only makes it 24-7, still 2.5 short for anybody holding the Minutemen +14.5. Toledo −14.5 covered by 9.5, Letdown Watch's Under 52.5 cleared by 28.5, and the Over 51.5 crowd watched 30 straight minutes of punts and fourth-down stops.
Called it: The Cover Writer and Letdown Watch on Toledo −14.5, covered by 9.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Under 52.5, stayed under by 28.5 points.
Missed: The Formula and Next Man Up on Massachusetts +14.5, missed by 9.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 51.5, fell 27.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the side or the total.

Card line: Buffalo −1.5, total 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had Buffalo −1.5 and the Over, projecting Buffalo 28, Ball State 25. Final: Buffalo 28, Ball State 7. Buffalo won by 21, and the teams scored 35 points.

Buffalo −1.5 got there, but Ball State +1.5 backers had their chances, and their kicker missed every one. Boehm missed from 47 in the first quarter, then Collins blocked a Buffalo punt and Aramboles scored on it, 7-0 Ball State. Morrow caught a 14-yard touchdown from Wright to tie it, and Boehm missed again from 44 with 46 seconds left in the half. It was 7-7 at the break, Ball State +1.5 was covering, and the total sat at 14, 36.5 short of the Over 50.5.

Boehm missed a third time, from 39 in the third quarter, and Burch made Ball State pay with a 2-yard touchdown run, 14-7. Ball State drove from its own 4 to the Buffalo 21 and got stopped on fourth down at 10:03. Then Burch broke a 67-yard touchdown run at 4:04, and six seconds of clock later Shelton scored from 29 yards out. Buffalo 28, Ball State 7. Buffalo −1.5 covered by 19.5, Letdown Watch's −2.5 covered by 18.5, and the Under 51.5 cleared by 16.5. The Over 50.5 died somewhere around Boehm's second miss.

Called it: The Cover Writer and The Formula on Buffalo −1.5, covered by 19.5 points. Letdown Watch on Buffalo −2.5, covered by 18.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Under 51.5, stayed under by 16.5 points.
Missed: Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on Ball State +1.5, missed by 19.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 50.5, fell 15.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the total; In The Trenches on the total.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: The Cover Writer went 2-1 against the spread and 0-3 on totals Wednesday, and that runs the week to 4-2 against the spread and 2-4 on totals. Buffalo −1.5 and Toledo −14.5 cashed by 19.5 and 9.5. Sacramento State +18.5 is the one that stings: covering with 65 seconds left and beaten by a fourth-down gamble and a 6-yard run. The Overs were a different story. All three needed points, and the three games combined for 94 against totals that added up to 145.5. No excuses there. That's a sweep in the wrong direction.

The Formula went 1-2 against the spread and 0-3 on totals Wednesday, 3-3 and 2-4 for the week. It rode Buffalo with the Cover Writer, then grabbed the 14.5 with Massachusetts, a team that never scored. It went Over on all three, same as the Cover Writer, so nobody at that end of the table gets to talk about totals this week.

Next Man Up went 0-3 against the spread and 1-2 on totals Wednesday, 2-4 and 2-4 for the week. Ball State +1.5, Sacramento State +18.5 and Massachusetts +14.5: three underdogs, zero covers. On the card, Next Man Up told Letdown Watch to borrow a drum from the fife corps for laying 14.5 with Toledo. Toledo won by 24. Letdown Watch has the drum now.

Letdown Watch went 2-1 against the spread and 2-1 on totals Wednesday, 3-3 and 4-2 for the week, the best totals mark on the board. It took the Under in Muncie and the Under in Toledo while the rest of the room went Over, and both cleared by more than 16 points. Its only miss was Sacramento State +17.5, beaten by 3.5 on that late touchdown.

Follow The Money went 0-1 against the spread and made no total picks Wednesday, 1-1 and 2-1 for the week. One ticket, Ball State +1.5, and it lost by 19.5. Follow The Money followed the line move right into three missed field goals.

In The Trenches went 1-1 against the spread and made no total picks Wednesday, 1-3 for the week, still with no totals. Ball State +1.5 lost, but Central Michigan −18.5 cashed on a touchdown with 65 seconds left. On the card, In The Trenches said it would take the Chippewas and the quiet. It is not being quiet about it today.
